post.text:
Klarna replaced 700 agents. Then rehired.

Their CEO said it himself: cost became too dominant, quality dropped.
I see the same mistake in support consultancies. L1 ticket volume eats the retainer margin, so someone proposes "replace the team with a bot".

What actually works:

1. Automate the ticket, not the person. Order status, warranty proof, password resets: let AI close those. That is 60 to 70% of volume at most brands we audit.

2. Keep humans for judgement. Refund exceptions, angry VIPs, legal. One good human on the hard 30% beats five on the easy 70%.

3. Measure resolution, not deflection. Zendesk reported 1M Custom Agent runs in 7 weeks this month. The metric that matters is "was it solved", not "did we avoid a human".

Friday take: if your AI plan starts with headcount instead of ticket types, you are building Klarna 2025.

Agree or disagree? Name the one ticket type you would never hand to a bot.

(We build this at Product Labs. Comment "audit" and I will send you the 5-step ticket audit we run before anything goes live.)

self_comments: The number nobody measures: "where is my order" was 38% of volume at the last brand we audited. Automating one intent, not the team, cleared a third of the queue.
Curious: for those who run support, what is your cost per resolved ticket today? Most teams I ask have never calculated it.

carousel.title: Automate the ticket, not the team
carousel.subtitle: What Klarna's reversal teaches every support leader

slides.title: Klarna cut 700 agents
slides.body: Cost fell. Quality fell faster. In 2025 the CEO admitted it and started rehiring humans.

slides.title: The mistake is the unit
slides.body: They automated headcount. The unit of automation is a ticket type, not a person.

slides.title: Let AI close the boring 70%
slides.body: Order status, warranty proof, password resets, invoice copies. Predictable, repetitive, measurable.

slides.title: Keep humans for the hard 30%
slides.body: Refund exceptions, angry VIPs, legal. One sharp human here beats five on easy tickets.

slides.title: Measure resolution, not deflection
slides.body: "Was it solved" is the metric. Deflection just hides the ticket until it comes back angrier.

engagement_comments.creator: Allie K. Miller
engagement_comments.comment:
The adoption gap I see is permission, not tooling.
Teams ship 3x faster the week a VP says "you will not be blamed for trying".
Who owns that permission in most orgs you work with?

engagement_comments.creator: Ethan Mollick
engagement_comments.topic: how people actually use AI at work
engagement_comments.comment:
Your point about jagged capability shows up hard in support.
The same model that nails warranty claims fails a refund exception with a sad customer.
Do you see teams mapping that jagged edge before they automate, or after it bites?

engagement_comments.creator: Andrew Ng
engagement_comments.comment:
Agentic workflows win on the boring tickets first.
At most brands 60 to 70% of volume is order status and proof-of-purchase, perfect for a reflect-and-retry loop.
What is the smallest agentic loop you would recommend a support team start with?

engagement_comments.creator: Ruben Hassid
engagement_comments.comment:
The 360Brew shift makes this concrete: profile and post topic now have to match.
I tightened my headline to the one thing I post about and the dwell time doubled.
Do you still see template-style posts getting suppressed this month?

engagement_comments.creator: Zain Kahn
engagement_comments.comment:
Productivity gains stall when nobody owns the handoff.
AI drafts the reply, a human approves, and the approval queue becomes the new bottleneck.
Have you seen a team fix the approval step without just removing it?

engagement_comments.creator: Rowan Cheung
engagement_comments.comment:
Zendesk's 1M Custom Agent executions in 7 weeks is the stat of the month for support.
The interesting part: they are now reporting resolution, not deflection.
Is that metric shift showing up in the other vendor announcements you track?

engagement_comments.creator: Greg Isenberg
engagement_comments.comment:
Underrated niche: AI support for brands that honour lifetime warranties across 5 to 17 sales channels.
Every claim needs proof of purchase, photos and a model number, and the volume never stops.
Would you build that as a vertical product or a service first?

engagement_comments.creator: Lenny Rachitsky
engagement_comments.comment:
Support tickets are the cheapest product research most PMs ignore.
Tag the top 10 intents for 30 days and the roadmap writes itself.
Do the best PM teams you know own a support metric directly?

engagement_comments.creator: Ankur Warikoo
engagement_comments.comment:
Top 5 Indian IT firms added 17 net employees in 9 months, versus 17,764 the year before.
The jobs are moving to people who can run AI on real workflows, not just talk about it.
What is the first skill you would tell a 2nd-year engineer to build this month?

engagement_comments.creator: Kunal Shah
engagement_comments.comment:
Contrarian take back at you: AI will create more support tickets, not fewer.
Personal agents will contact businesses on behalf of customers, so volume rises while each ticket gets cheaper.
Which Indian consumer category feels that first?

dms.message: Thanks for the comment. Here is the 5-step ticket audit we run, no strings attached: 1) export 30 days of tickets, 2) tag the top 10 intents, 3) mark what needs judgement, 4) price a human reply (loaded cost ÷ tickets per hour), 5) automate one intent at a time and measure resolution weekly. Happy to look at your intent list if you want a second pair of eyes.

dms.to: someone who disagreed in the comments
dms.message: Appreciate you pushing back, that is the point of a Friday post. Genuinely curious which ticket type burned you with automation. I have seen refund exceptions go wrong more than anything else.

dms.to: a support leader who liked the post
dms.message: Saw you engaged with the Klarna post. One thing I did not fit in: the teams that kept quality measured cost per resolved ticket before and after. If you want the one-line formula we use, it is loaded cost ÷ resolved tickets per hour. Nothing to sell, just useful.
Thanks for the repost. If any of your clients sell managed support, the L1 margin point tends to land hard with them. Happy to share the one-page version you can forward.

dms.to: a recruiter or hiring manager who viewed the profile
dms.message: Noticed you stopped by my profile after the Klarna post. If you are figuring out where AI fits in a support team, I am glad to share what we have seen work (and what did not). No pitch.
